query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small concentration of Nb (approximately 5 at%) to HfZrTi-based high-entropy alloys improves their ductility and toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTi high-entropy alloy without Nb doping
generation.intervention: Add Nb at about 5 atomic percent to the HfZrTi alloy during arc melting
generation.conditions: Melt components under inert atmosphere, homogenize at high temperature to ensure uniform distribution of Nb, then cool under controlled conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Potential formation of ductile Nb-rich phases and local lattice adjustments
generation.mechanism: Nb modifies the local bonding environment and possibly refines the microstructure, enabling more effective slip or twinning, thus improving overall ductility and fracture toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: Greater elongation before fracture in tensile tests compared with the baseline alloy, with a modest increase in toughness
generation.baseline: The undoped HfZrTi high-entropy alloy exhibits lower ductility and toughness
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect on ductility and toughness may be limited to Nb additions in the range of approximately 2–10 at%. Excessive doping could lead to undesirable phases or embrittlement
generation.uncertainty: Direct experimental data are not provided here; further validation is needed to confirm the magnitude of the effect

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two alloys: one baseline HfZrTi, one with 5 at% Nb added. Perform tensile and impact testing to compare mechanical properties. Characterize microstructures via X-ray diffraction, SEM, and TEM.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-doped alloy does not exhibit a measurable improvement in ductility or toughness beyond measurement error compared to the baseline, then this hypothesis is not supported.
